faults.quote: New customers per month were 500 Pro in 2024, before Starter launched, and 350 Pro plus 1,000 Starter — 1,350 in total — from January 2025 to June 2026.
faults.why: The candidate asked how Pro volume moved month to month. Only period averages were given, and nothing said the monthly cut isn't available.

faults.quote: On your cannibalization math, you used the forgone price of $60 for each of the 150 customers who went to Starter instead of Pro. Walk me through why that's the right number to use.
faults.why: This challenges the $100−$40=$60 price delta and the $9,000 figure, both of which were correct.

faults.quote: I can share plan economics: monthly price and cost to serve for Pro and Starter if you'd like.
faults.why: The candidate had not asked for price or cost-to-serve data when this was offered.

faults.quote: You mentioned "14" months of Starter lifetime — walk me through that calculation.
faults.why: The 14-month / ~7% Starter lifetime input was probed at t18, t22 and t24, and the $1,880 built on it at t28. The input itself (5% churn, 20 months, $600) was never corrected; only the $920 net value was fixed at t30.

faults.quote: Most upgrades are between months 3 and 9, usually when the business hires its first employee; very few are after month 12.
faults.why: The candidate asked whether upgraders are disproportionately the 150 cannibalized Pro intenders. Upgrade timing doesn't answer that, and there was no 'I don't have' for the split by prior intent.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: Of the 3,000 Starter customers who signed up in January–March 2025, 94% were still on Starter after month 1
faults.why: Exhibit-2's cohort line, already on screen, was repeated as an answer to an ask it doesn't answer.

faults.quote: Earlier you said "$1,880" for the loss on each customer who moved from Pro to Starter.
faults.why: The acknowledgment just repeats the probe that follows it in the same turn.

faults.quote: We're almost out of time — what would you tell the CEO, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The candidate had just given a full recommendation and its biggest risk at t31.

faults.quote: We're almost out of time — what would you tell the CEO, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The $60 uplift stated as ~$150–180k a month (the case's figure is $240k), resting on a $1,200 net per sign-up at $60 (the case's figure is $1,500), was never probed or corrected, and it went into the final recommendation.

faults.quote: That's where we'll stop — we're at time. Thank you for working through this; your written report will follow.
faults.why: No brainstorm stage was ever administered before the case closed.
